many books.
And there are found twenty-five books of Hunayn,
apart from those which he translated from Greek into Syriac and into Arabic.
And he had a sister's son whose name was Hubaysh bar Hasan, "the Lame-Handed",
likewise a wonderful translator of medical books.
And from the good fortune of Hunayn,
most of the books that this Hubaysh translated,
when those weak in knowledge came upon them,
they thought that they were by Hunayn,
and that the scribe had made an error in the letters of the name.
And they would erase Hubaysh
and write Hunayn.
And for this reason, few are the books that remained under the name of Hubaysh,
and the rest are mostly written under the name of Hunayn.
After al-Muhtadi, al-Mu'tamid son of al-Mutawakkil [ruled] twenty-three years.
This man, during all of his reign {OCR?}, was occupied with war against that rebel who had arisen in the south.
And in the year 265
of the Arabs [878–879 AD], the Romans took from the Arabs the fortress of Lulwah (Lulqah) (Lulwan?).
And after a year, Bar Rashid, the general of the Arabs, gathered four thousand horsemen
and entered the territory of the Romans.
And the patricians of the Romans came against him:
he of Seleucia,
and he of Tyana,
and he of Charsianon,
and others;
and they surrounded {OCR?} the force of the Arabs.
Then the Arabs, having cut off hope of life,
dismounted from their horses,
and hamstrung all of them,
and knelt on their knees,
and began shooting arrows at the Romans.
Yet their shooting did not avail them,
but they {the Romans} fell upon them, upon the Arabs,
and killed some of them,
and bound some of them, together with Bar Rashid, their leader.
And in the year 270
of the Arabs [883–884 AD], Ishaq {OCR?}, general of the Arabs, gathered a large army and marched against the rebel who was in the south,
some of them in ships and some by dry land.
And after a great struggle,
they prevailed over him and defeated the rebel's force,
and killed him between the rivers of Babylon.
For that Ali said not only that he was descended from the prophet of the Arabs,
but he also proclaimed that he was a prophet.
And [he claimed] that on a certain day, while dwelling in the wilderness,
a cloud overshadowed him,
